title: Retinal Masterclass: Vascular, Degenerative & Hereditary Disorders
summary: An exhaustive clinical guide to the diagnosis and management of retinal pathologies, ranging from Diabetic Retinopathy and Vascular Occlusions to complex Hereditary Dystrophies. This visual compendium integrates international study protocols with gold-standard diagnostic criteria.

rows: Any or all: Microaneurysm, retinal hge, exudates, cotton wool spot up to level of moderate
Review range 6-12m (Depends on: severity of signs, stability, systemic factors, personal circumstances)

- Severe retinal hge (20 medium-large/quadrant in 1-3 quadrants) or mild IRMA
- Significant venous beading in no more than 1 quadrant
- Cotton wool spots
Review in 6m (PDR in up to 26%, High risk in up to 8% within a year)

One or more of:
- Severe hge in 4 quadrants
- Significant venous beading in 2+ quadrants
- Moderate IRMA in 1+ quadrants
Review in 4 months (PDR up to 50%, High risk up to 15% within a year)
One or more criteria for severe NPDR
Review in 2-3 months (High risk PDR up to 45% within a year)
NVD’s or NVE’s but extent insufficient to meet high-risk criteria
Treatment depends on severity, stability, systemic factors, reliability. Review up to 2 months if not treated.

- NVD > 1/3 disc area
- NVD + Vitreous Hge (VH)
- NVE > 1/2 disc area with VH
Immediately if possible in same day

sections.title: Critical PDR Characteristics & Neovascularization
content: B. Presence of any active neovascularization
C. Location of neovascularization on or within one disc diameter of optic disc
D. NVD > 1/3 disc area or NVE > 1/2 disc area

sections.title: ETDRS: Clinically Significant Macular Oedema (CSME)
content: A. Retinal thickening within 500 micrometer or 1/3 disc diameter of the centre of the macula
B. Hard exudates within 500 micrometer of the centre of the macula with adjacent retinal thickening which may lie > 500 micrometer from foveal center
C. Retinal thickening 1DD area any part of which within one disc diameter of the centre of the macula

branches: General: Education, weight reduction, exercise, compliance
Medical: Fenofibrate 200 mg, Address Anaemia/Renal Failure
Anti-VEGF Agents: Ranibizumab, Aflibercept, Bevacizumab, Faricimab
Steroids: Triamcinolone or Sustained Release Implants (Pregnancy/Anti-VEGF contraindications)

rows: IV Ranibizumab > focal grid laser for CI-DME; laser should be deferred 6m after anti-VEGF start.
No VA diff at 5y between drugs; however, Aflibercept better if baseline VA is 6/15 or worse.
IV Ranibizumab injections as effective as photocoagulation (PRP) for high-risk PDR at 5 years.
Intravitreal Aflibercept injections are as effective as PRP.
Vitrectomy + PRP recovers vision faster than Aflibercept, but VA similar at 2 years.
Faricimab 6mg: 4 initial injections then Treat & Extend.
In patients with PDR + Macular Edema: Treat edema then undertake PRP.

sections.title: Laser Photocoagulation Parameters
content: Lenses: Panfundiscopic, Mainster, Area Centralis
PRP Spot Size: 400μm (Interface selection determines retinal diameter)
Focal Laser Spot: 50-100μm, 500-3000μm from foveola
Duration: 0.05-0.1 sec (PRP), 0.02-1 sec (Focal)
Power: Light intensity burn; Spacing: 1-1.5 burn width
PRP Dosage: 1500 (initial), 2500-3500 (Mild PDR), 4000 (Moderate), 7000 (Severe PDR)
Modified grid laser: No longer recommended
Technique: Treat lower fundus first in severe PDR; avoid vitreoretinal traction areas

sections.title: Regression Indicators (Post-Laser)
content: 1. Blunting of vessel tips
2. Shrinking and disappearance of NV
3. Regression of IRMA
4. Decrease in venous changes
5. Absorption of retinal hemorrhages
6. Disc pallor

sections.title: Indications for Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV)
content: Severe persistent vitreous hemorrhage
Progressive tractional retinal detachment (TRD)
Combined tractional rhegmatogenous RD
Premacular retrohyaloid hemorrhage
Anterior segment neovascularization with media opacities

branches: Ischaemic CRVO Signs: VA <6/60, RAPD, deep hemorrhages, multiple CWS, FA >10DD non-perfusion, reduced ERG b-wave
Previous CRVO Signs: Collaterals, Telangiectatic bed, Venous dilation/tortuosity, Perivenous sheathing, Macular changes
Systemic Associations: HTN, DM, Hyperlipidemia, Hyperhomocysteinaemia, Blood disorders (Myeloma, Leukemia), Inflammatory (Behcet, SLE, Sarcoid), Glaucoma, Short axial length
RVO Studies: BRAVO (Ranibizumab > Laser), VIBRANT (Aflibercept PRN), CRUISE/COPERNICUS (Ranibizumab/Aflibercept monthly), COMRADE (Ranibizumab > Dexamethasone), SCORE (Triamcinolone > Control)

rows: Smoking, Pulse (AF), BP, Murmurs, ECG, ESR/CRP/FBC (GCA), FBS, Lipid profile, Carotid duplex.
Specialist stroke clinic referral, Antiplatelet (600mg Aspirin load), Warfarin, Carotid endarterectomy (if >70% stenosis).
Ocular massage (3-mirror, 3-5 mins), AC paracentesis, Apraclonidine 1%, Timolol 0.5%, IV Acetazolamide 500mg.
Amaurosis Fugax: Transient painless monocular loss (Embolic, Hemodynamic, Ocular, Neurologic, Idiopathic).
Thrombolysis: IV tPA Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (10% over 1m, 90% over 59m).
Rebreathing/Carbogen: Elevate CO2 to promote vasodilation and retard ischaemia.

sections.title: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP)
content: Screening Criteria: Born ≤ 30-32 weeks OR Weight ≤ 1500g OR Severe illness
Timing: Start 4-7 weeks postnatally; review 1-3 week intervals
Discharge Criteria: Vascularization reaches Zone 3
Type 1 Treatment (within 72h): Stage 3 in Zone 1; Any stage + Plus in Zone 1; Stage 2/3 in Zone 2 + Plus disease

rows: PCV, Exudative AMD, RAP (Type 3 MNV), Chronic CSR, Posterior Uveitis, Choroidal Tumors, Bruch's breaks, FA contraindication.
MNV detection (flow in outer retina), Non-exudative MNV, DR (Preretinal NV vs IRMA), Microvascular changes, Deep capillary plexus in DME.
ABCA4 gene, dark choroid on FA

sections.title: MNV Studies & New Therapeutics
sections.content:
Trials: MARINA/ANCHOR (Ranibizumab efficacy), PIER/HORIZON/PRONTO/HARBOUR (Dosing strategies), CATT/IVAN (Ranibizumab vs Bevacizumab), VIEW1/2 (Aflibercept), LUCERNE/TENAYA (Faricimab). 

New Drugs:
- Brolucizumab (Beavu): Smaller, high binding affinity, 3-monthly dosing.
- Faricimab (Vabysmo): Bispecific (Ang-2 + VEGF-A), up to 16w dosing.

rows: AR, ABCA4 (1p). Mottling, ﬂecks (snail slime/bronze), atrophy.
FA: Dark Choroid. FAF: Hyper-autoﬂuorescent ﬂecks. ERG: Photopic normal, scotopic subnormal.
EOG: Severely subnormal (Arden Index <1.5) even in carriers.
Signs: Scalloped chorioretinal atrophy, crystals, PSC cataract. Rx: Arginine-restricted diet, B6.

sections.title: Myopia & Bruch's Membrane Pathology
content: Degenerative Myopia: Pale tesselated fundus, Lacquer cracks, Fuchs spot, Staphyloma, MNV, Macular retinoschisis.
Systemic Myopia: Down, Stickler, Marfan, Ehlers-Danlos, Pierre Robin, Noonan syndromes.
Angioid Streaks: Crack-like dehiscence in calcified Bruch's. Links: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum, Paget's, Sickle cell, Ehlers-Danlos (no link).
Choroidal Folds Causes: Idiopathic, Papilledema (elevated ICP), Orbital tumors, Posterior scleritis, Hypotony.

sections.title: Electrophysiology (ERG/EOG) Definitions
content: ERG A-wave: Fast negative, from photoreceptors.
ERG B-wave: Large positive, from Muller & Bipolar cells (integrity measure).
ERG C-wave: Negative, from RPE-Photoreceptors.
Implicit Time: Stimulus to B-wave peak.
EOG Arden Ratio: Light peak / Dark trough (> 1.7 is normal). Refelcts RPE/Photoreceptor activity.

branches: CSR Risks: H.pylori, Dialysis, HTN, Stress, Steroids, Sleep Apnea
CSR Management: Observation, Stop steroids, Spironolactone 40mg, Micropulse Laser, PDT
PCV Risks: Smoking, BMI, increased CRP
CME Causes: Post-op, Uveitis, Prostaglandin drops, RP, ERM, MNV, Renal failure
Systemic Hypotony: Dehydration, Hyperglycaemia, Uraemia, CAIs
